import LinearAlgebra.Matrix.CharPoly
import Algebra.Lie.Algebra
import Algebra.Lie.Subalgebra
import Algebra.Lie.Module
import Data.Nat.TrailingDegree

open LieAlgebra
open LieSubalgebra

theorem lg_target (K : Type u_7) {L : Type u_8} [Field K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [Module.Finite K L] (x : L) : 
  Module.finrank K ↥(LieSubalgebra.engel K x) = (LinearMap.charpoly ((LieAlgebra.ad K L) x)).natTrailingDegree := by
  let engel_subalgebra := LieSubalgebra.engel K x
  let ad_x := LieAlgebra.ad K L x
  let dim_engel := Module.finrank K ↥engel_subalgebra

  -- Show that ad_x is nilpotent on the Engel subalgebra
  have h_ad_nilpotent : ad_x ^ dim_engel = 0 :=
    by
      let n := dim_engel
      have : ∀ i ≥ n, ad_x ^ i = 0 :=
        by
          apply LieSubalgebra.mem_engel_iff.1
          exact ⟨n, by simp [ad_x, pow]⟩
      rw [this]
      exact Nat.le_refl _

  -- Use the fact that the characteristic polynomial of a nilpotent operator has trailing degree equal to its dimension
  have h_charpoly_trailing_degree : (LinearMap.charpoly ad_x).natTrailingDegree = dim_engel :=
    by
      have h_ad_nilpotent' : ad_x.isNilpotent :=
        by
          rw [isNilpotent]
          exact h_ad_nilpotent
      have h_charpoly_trailing_degree' : (LinearMap.charpoly ad_x).natTrailingDegree = (LinearMap.dim ad_x).toNat :=
        by
          rw [LinearMap.charpoly_natTrailingDegree]
          exact h_ad_nilpotent'
      rw [h_charpoly_trailing_degree']
      exact rfl

  -- Conclude the equality
  exact h_charpoly_trailing_degree
